data.name: Nikolaos
data.gender_notes: Nikolaos is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'nikos' meaning victory and 'laos' meaning people. In Christian tradition, Saint Nicholas is a symbol of victory over sin and evil. The name Nikolaos carries the meaning “Victory of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nikolaos usually hope their child will grow to embody victory of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carries the symbolic message of triumph over adversity and faith in the power of God.
data.etymology: Nikolaos belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nikolaos total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
data.cultural_impact: Saint Nicholas is popularly known as Santa Claus, the jolly figure who brings gifts to children during Christmas Eve. His legacy has influenced Christmas traditions and gift-giving culture across the world.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, Saint Nicholas is venerated as a saint and a bishop in the early Christian church in Myra, present-day Demre in Turkey. He is the patron saint of children, students, merchants, and archers, and is another manifestation of Jesus Christ's love and compassion towards children. Saint Nicholas is known for his generosity, secret gift-giving, and helping those in need. His feast day on December 6 is still celebrated with gift-giving, charitable acts, and community gatherings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Nikolaos carries profound spiritual symbolism as it is rooted in Biblical tradition. As a name associated with Saint Saint Nicholas of Myra, it represents holiness, devotion, and Christian virtue. biblical_reference.note: Nikolaos was a member of the first seven deacons appointed by the apostles in Jerusalem. He was also the companion of Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Nikolaos of Myra was a bishop of Myra in Lycia, Anatolia, during the late 4th century. The name Nikolaos carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Nikolaos was known for his generosity and miracles, and is the patron saint of sailors, merchants, archers, students, and children.
